title: Gemina: A Coordinated and High-Performance Memory Deduplication Engine
problem: Memory deduplication (via KSM) eliminates duplicate pages but forces huge pages to split into 4KB base pages, degrading TLB hit rates and memory access performance by up to 43%; asynchronous huge page promotion cannot recover this loss because deduplication breaks the uniformity of page attributes required for promotion.
motivation: Huge pages are critical for TLB efficiency in modern servers, and deduplication is essential for memory overcommit in cloud/VM environments, but their interaction is fundamentally conflicted and degrades both memory savings and access performance simultaneously.
method: Gemina coordinates huge page management with memory deduplication through three components: (1) a fine-grained detector that separately classifies pages by both redundancy and access hotness to decouple deduplication decisions from page-size decisions; (2) a distributor that conservatively processes pages to avoid frequent hot/cold and size-class switches; and (3) an adapter that reorganizes memory layout to enable fast base-to-huge-page conversion. Together, these components preserve huge page availability by selectively deferring or avoiding deduplication of hot pages while still capturing most memory savings.
key_novelty: Jointly optimizing memory deduplication and huge page management through a coordinated three-component system that preserves huge page promotability while retaining near-full deduplication savings.
contributions: Fine-grained detector classifying pages by both redundancy and hotness for coordinated policy decisions
Conservative distributor preventing frequent page-attribute state transitions
Memory adapter enabling fast huge page reconstruction after selective deduplication
96.1% of KSM memory savings while recovering 43.1% of access performance lost in naive KSM

metrics.other: 96.1% of KSM memory savings retained; 43.1% memory access performance improvement vs. naive KSM-based deduplication

limitations: The overhead of the hotness/redundancy detector and adapter on overall system throughput under high churn workloads is not quantified in the abstract.
primary_theme: Coordinated huge-page-aware memory deduplication to recover TLB performance
